Simulated raw marker data for a diversity panel

Source: R/genoGWASsim.R
genoGWASraw.Rd

A simulated diversity-panel genotype dataset used by the GWAS vignettes to demonstrate the complete data-preparation workflow checkPanel() -> filterPanel() -> primePanel(). The panel comprises 200 diversity lines genotyped at approximately 1700 SNP markers spread across 10 chromosomes at approximately 0.9 cM average spacing (chromosome length ~150 cM). All markers on the panel have minor allele frequency (MAF) greater than 0.15 – rare variants are excluded at the sampling stage (AlphaSimR addSnpChip(minSnpFreq = 0.15)) with a belt-and-braces post-random- mating filter – so the panel is dominated by informative common variants with a healthy MAF spread (median MAF ~0.32). Genotypes are stored in raw 0/1/2 allele-count coding exactly as they would be received from a genotyping facility.

The dataset deliberately contains a range of realistic data-quality issues so that the panel-preparation functions can be demonstrated end-to-end. The embedded issues are:

Missingness

Approximately 2% baseline missingness across all cells, plus about 150 markers with 25–40% missingness (failed genotyping assays) and 5 lines with 22–35% missingness (poor-quality DNA).

Monomorphic markers

Fifteen markers forced to a single allele (MAF = 0).

Duplicate lines

Four pairs of lines with identical genotype profiles (accidentally submitted twice).

Duplicate markers

Approximately 40 pairs of markers with identical genotype vectors (very-close markers in perfect LD or re-assayed loci). The observed count in checkPanel() is typically slightly higher because of natural duplicates arising from the LD structure.

Unplaceable markers

Twenty-five markers renamed SNP_UNPLACED_001..SNP_UNPLACED_025 so they no longer match any entry in mapGWASsim; these are dropped by the map-consistency step of filterPanel().

Low-MAF markers

None below the 0.15 sampling floor. The default filterPanel() MAF filter (0.05) is therefore a no-op on this panel, but is still worth running for real datasets.

The panel is drawn as a single genetically diverse population with no discrete subpopulation structure. Within each chromosome, marker genotypes are generated from an AR(1) latent liability with \(\lambda = 3\) cM, giving realistic LD decay (\(r(\Delta = 1\,\text{cM}) \approx 0.72\), \(r(\Delta = 3\,\text{cM}) \approx 0.37\)) but no cross-chromosome correlations beyond what is captured by the whole-genome kinship matrix \(K\). This is deliberate: earlier versions injected independent per-chromosome subpopulation liability shifts, which produced within-chromosome subpop signal stronger than \(K\)'s cross-chromosome average and confounded the multi-environment GWAS with spurious hits on whichever chromosome drew the largest subpop offsets.

Five QTL were planted to drive detectable signal in the yield phenotype phenoGWASsim (see that page for details). All five QTL markers survive the default filterPanel() step so the GWAS pipeline can recover them from the prepared panel.

Usage

genoGWASraw

Format

A data.frame with 200 rows (one per diversity line) and approximately 1700 columns (1 id column plus one column per marker; the exact marker count varies slightly across regenerations depending on how many markers drift below the 0.15 MAF floor after 1 generation of random mating):

id

Character. Line identifier ("Line001" to "Line200").

SNP_C01_0001, SNP_C01_0002, ...

Integer. Raw genotype values in 0/1/2 allele-count coding (0 = AA homozygote, 1 = AB heterozygote, 2 = BB homozygote, NA = missing). Marker names follow the pattern SNP_C<chr>_<index>. Twenty-five columns are renamed SNP_UNPLACED_001..SNP_UNPLACED_025 to simulate markers absent from the genetic map.

See also

mapGWASsim, phenoGWASsim, checkPanel, filterPanel, primePanel, gwasAim

Examples

data(genoGWASraw,  package = "wgAim")
data(mapGWASsim,   package = "wgAim")

dim(genoGWASraw)         # 200 x ~1700
#> [1]  200 1692
genoGWASraw[1:5, 1:6]
#>              id SNP_C01_0001 SNP_C01_0002 SNP_C01_0003 SNP_C01_0004
#> Line001 Line001            0            1            2            1
#> Line002 Line002            0            1            2            1
#> Line003 Line003            0            0            1            0
#> Line004 Line004            0            0            2            0
#> Line005 Line005            0            1            1            1
#>         SNP_C01_0005
#> Line001            2
#> Line002            2
#> Line003            2
#> Line004            2
#> Line005            1

# Diagnose the embedded issues
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
chk <- checkPanel(genoGWASraw, mapGWASsim, id = "id")
print(chk)
} # }
